root_cause.text: The `hbh_mt6_check()` function in the netfilter `ip6t_hbh` module fails to validate the `optsnr` field from userspace, allowing a value larger than the fixed-size `opts[IP6T_OPTS_OPTSNR]` array (size 16), which leads to an out-of-bounds array access during packet matching.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a bounds check `if (optsinfo->optsnr > IP6T_OPTS_OPTSNR) return -EINVAL;` and the CVE description confirms that `optsnr` can exceed `IP6T_OPTS_OPTSNR` (16), resulting in an off-by-one access at index 16 as reported by UBSAN.

vuln_statements.explanation: Assigns the optsnr field from user-controlled packet data to the info structure without any bounds check, setting up the index for later array access.
Directly uses the unchecked optsnr value as an index into the opts array (size 16), causing out-of-bounds access when optsnr exceeds 15.
Assignment to the opts array at an index determined by optsnr without prior validation, leading to out-of-bounds write if optsnr is too large.
Loop iterating based on optsnr without capping its value, potentially causing excessive array access or OOB reads when optsnr is larger than the array size.
Declaration of the fixed-size opts array (size 16) that, combined with the missing bounds check on optsnr, makes OOB accesses possible.
